summary: Creates a first, deliberately thin Student Experience Hub: a shared student home and reusable app foundation, with King’s Edge as the first deep product domain and light-touch access to timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s.
detailSummary:
The Student App and Journey Integration deliverable owns the Student Experience Hub as a student-facing product and shared technical platform. Its September 2027 first release is deliberately modest: it should give students one useful place to start, demonstrate the institutional direction of travel and establish reusable app foundations without turning each underlying service into a new integration project in year one.

King’s Edge remains the substantive product build. The Hub will present that experience natively while giving students coherent access to timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s at the lightest depth that creates useful value. Where a reliable existing feed or widget is straightforward, information may be surfaced directly. Where it is not, the Hub can provide a clear authenticated hand-off, deep link or service entry point. The first release does not require King’s to recreate source-system functionality, expose every piece of available data or complete the wider CRM transformation under 4.1.1.

The first-year product work therefore concentrates on the common home, identity and navigation, accessible interaction patterns, basic telemetry and the small amount of integration needed to make the four domains feel coherent. Technical and service discovery should confirm the simplest safe access pattern for each source rather than seeking the deepest possible integration. Student testing should be proportionate and continuous, focused on whether the Hub makes everyday navigation clearer and whether the common home is worth returning to.

The wider Hub can then deepen iteratively. Live evidence from the first release, continued journey research, the maturity of 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems and the readiness of 4.1.1 should determine where deeper end-to-end integration is genuinely valuable.

caseForChange.problem:
Students currently encounter King’s through a fragmented collection of portals, applications, websites and organisational routes. Information and functionality are structured around the systems and teams that provide them rather than around what a student is trying to do. Even common daily needs such as seeing a timetable, entering learning spaces, finding opportunities or asking for support require students to know which destination to use.

King’s therefore lacks a single useful place from which a student can begin their digital day. This fragmentation weakens the value of services and information that already exist, creates avoidable cognitive effort and particularly disadvantages students who are less familiar with institutional structures or less able to rely on informal knowledge.

The underlying digital estate will not become simple quickly. Core systems, data foundations and service platforms will continue to change over several years. Waiting for that transformation before creating a coherent student-facing experience would defer visible benefit, while building only a deep King’s Edge product would miss the opportunity to establish the shared front door from the outset.
caseForChange.opportunity:
The Student Experience Hub can establish a useful horizontal layer across the existing estate without requiring deep integration with every source from the start.

The September 2027 release can focus on a simple common home spanning King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s. King’s Edge provides the deep native experience. The other sources can be represented through the simplest safe and useful pattern available, including a live feed or widget where already feasible, or a clear authenticated hand-off or deep link where that is more proportionate.

This allows King’s to demonstrate a coherent student-facing direction, establish reusable app foundations and learn from real use while avoiding premature re-engineering of services and systems that are themselves still changing.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is already moving into rapid replatforming and substantial product development, creating a practical opportunity to establish the shared application foundations from which a wider Hub can grow.

The conversation with senior education leadership has also created a clear expectation that this work should begin to look and feel like the start of a wider student hub rather than a standalone Edge destination. September 2027 is a useful point to make that direction visible.

The opportunity is to do that proportionately. A thin shared home can create real student value and institutional learning without requiring year one to absorb the cost and risk of several deep integration projects at once.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
From September 2027, students have one coherent digital place from which to begin their day at King’s.

The Student Experience Hub provides a shared home and navigation layer. King’s Edge is available as the first substantive native product domain, while timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s are present through clear, useful access routes at a depth proportionate to what can be delivered safely and simply.

The common shell, identity, navigation, accessible design patterns and telemetry are designed for reuse. Broader student journeys can then be integrated progressively as evidence, service readiness and system capability justify the additional effort, including deeper CRM-enabled support journeys as 4.1.1 matures.

Over time, the Hub can move from coherent access and navigation towards more personalised and integrated end-to-end experiences, but the September 2027 release is primarily the credible beginning of that journey.

benefits.title: Students have one useful place to start their day
benefits.statement: A common student home brings together clear routes to timetable, learning, support and King’s Edge, reducing the need to remember and navigate separate institutional destinations.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the September 2027 first release, strengthening as the Hub deepens
benefits.successLooksLike: Students can use the Hub as a useful starting point and reach common daily destinations with fewer dead ends and less dependence on institutional knowledge.

benefits.title: Access to provision becomes more equitable
benefits.statement: A consistent digital starting point and clearer discovery routes make services, learning information and opportunities more visible to students who are less able to rely on informal knowledge, confidence or existing networks.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, particularly those currently less well served by fragmented provision
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first release, increasing as personalisation and integration mature
benefits.successLooksLike: Relevant provision reaches a broader range of students and differences in discovery, navigation or take-up between student groups begin to narrow.

benefits.title: King’s creates a reusable student-home and app foundation
benefits.statement: A shared shell, identity, navigation and product pattern allow King’s to create immediate student value from existing services while providing a credible base for deeper journeys later.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, product teams and King’s
benefits.owner: TBC – Student Experience Hub product and platform owner
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first live Hub release and as common capabilities are reused
benefits.successLooksLike: New student-facing requirements can reuse the Hub foundations where appropriate, and deeper integration is added selectively rather than through repeated standalone products.

steps.title: Establish the shared app architecture and platform foundations
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish the minimum shared architecture, hosting, identity, navigation, telemetry and service foundations needed for the King’s Edge replatform and a thin Student Experience Hub home.

steps.title: Confirm the minimum first-release access patterns
steps.summary: From September to December 2026, confirm the simplest safe and useful way for the September 2027 Hub to represent King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s. Default to existing feeds, widgets, authenticated hand-offs or deep links rather than bespoke integration unless deeper work is clearly justified.

steps.title: Prototype the thin common student home
steps.summary: From November 2026 to April 2027, test increasingly realistic versions of the shared home with students, focusing on information hierarchy, navigation, the relationship between King’s Edge and the three lighter-touch service routes, and whether the Hub is genuinely useful as a starting point.

steps.title: Build the shared Hub shell alongside King’s Edge
steps.summary: From January to June 2027, build the common home, identity, navigation, profile and telemetry while the deeper King’s Edge product develops under 4.1.4. Add only the light-touch timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s access needed for the first release.

steps.title: Test the working Hub with students and service owners
steps.summary: From March to June 2027, put the working common home in front of a bounded but varied student cohort and the relevant service owners. Test usefulness, clarity, accessibility and hand-offs, and use the evidence to refine the September release.

steps.title: Lock the September first-release scope
steps.summary: By the end of June 2027, confirm the minimum September scope and resist additions that would turn the thin Hub into several new integration projects.

steps.title: Complete proportionate launch readiness
steps.summary: During July and August 2027, complete the security, privacy, accessibility, performance, monitoring, support and release-readiness work appropriate to the actual first-release scope, while protecting King’s Edge service continuity.

steps.title: Launch the first Student Experience Hub
steps.summary: Launch in September 2027 with a shared student home, King’s Edge as the substantive native experience, and clear light-touch access to timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s.

steps.title: Operate, learn and decide where deeper integration is worth it
steps.summary: From September 2027 to February 2028, use live evidence to improve the common home and identify where deeper integration would create enough student value to justify additional product, service and technical effort.

steps.title: Approve the deeper app roadmap and first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: From March to April 2028, combine live Hub evidence, systems and information-flow evidence, student-journey research and learning from King’s Edge to select the first non-Edge areas that should move beyond access and hand-off into deeper integrated journeys.

steps.title: Deepen the shared app with the first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: Build the first selected deeper journeys into the existing student home, connecting authoritative data and CRM-enabled interactions where ready while retaining source systems where they continue to add specialist value.

steps.title: Expand integrated journeys and common app capabilities
steps.summary: Add further priority journeys and mature common search, actions, communications, notifications, personalisation, self-service and system integration, progressively replacing shallow hand-offs where deeper integration adds clear value.

steps.title: Make wider student journeys the primary product roadmap
steps.summary: Shift the centre of product demand towards the broader student experience, integrate additional systems and service journeys, and use common Hub capabilities to help students navigate information, opportunities, actions, progress and support through a more coherent institutional relationship.

steps.title: Consolidate the Hub and rationalise parallel entry points
steps.summary: Establish the Student Experience Hub as the primary student-facing product and platform, with enduring product ownership, platform governance, service management, cost ownership and product analytics. Progressively retire or rationalise duplicated portals and repeated functionality where continuity is assured, while retaining specialist source systems and interfaces where they continue to add necessary value.
